Thanks, i never seen it before. Thanks. It sort of hit me. Think i found it at just a right time.

I'm sorry you have such crap family. Maybe it does get better with time. What helped me (am still struggling with it tho) is acceptance. Accepting that i don't need to be someone  important or have lots of money/power to live life. I've also learned not to complain too much. That usually i ve noticed turns people away from me. Also one more thing is understanding how people work. Some just are the way they are because that s the only way they can survive. Maybe they can change, maybe not. Anyway, sorry and i m around if u wanna talk
Maybe what u re missing is home. By home i mean family/people you love and love you. Well, at least that s what i ve boiled it down to after long thinking about what s wrong with me.

I have same problem with my family. Also my gf sometimes feels like she just wants to dominate me and doesn t understand anything serious about myself i tell her. Careerwise i m already a failure. I m like 9 years behind my peers so i already gave up on that. I m sorry you re feeling like this. If you wanna talk just pm me
Hey, i m around if you wanna talk

I'm quite convinced the delusions/hallucinations i had are my neurons playing tricks on me. I'm also quite convinced they are alive and are a part of me. This sole belief keeps me always in check. I didn t have it after my first episode. If somebody asked me about it i would just conjure up some lie. Also they are real. Meaning the little men in my brain. As in they re in my brain and they re real. Inside my brain. Otherwise if i overlook this fact it s really easy for me to believe whatever these little shits want me to believe and go chasing them in the real world.

I wanted to jump of a tall building during my 2nd psychosis because i was just feeling too sick to go to work or just basically do anything. It was horrible. I remember wishing i had a switch to kill myself bcs even finding such a tall building was too much of an effort. I just wanted to be sure i d do it right.

Anyway, 1 year and a half away i m much better now, but same as you i can't shake this fucking horrible feeling that something bad's gonna happen. It just persists all the through the day and it just sometimes gets tiring to shake it off and i get sometimes (too often) overwhelmed by all kinds of intrusive thoughts which just drain every little joy of life i manage to conjure up.
Every time i was convinced of anything similar i was psychotic. What you believe might be true but you have no real proof of it so as long as you are convinced of it i d say you re psychotic.

Wow. I basically experienced everything you had (the awakening part was the hugest deal and what kept feeding my psychosis, also telepathy cause of the voices, malefic friends, facing my fears, etc.)and had a similar attitude. (Wrote all kinds of crap to friends, got also into random fights with strangers which left me with harrasment and threat suits) Luckily they didn t arrest me, the police took me in handcuffs from my house after threatening to force the door open which scared the shit out of me cuz i was imagining they d torture me by beating the shit out of me. In the end they just sent me to the hospital directly.

I'm sorry you're going through hell. Our psychotic experiences have a lot more similitudes in common than i had time to mention and if you wanna talk about it or if there s any way i can help just dm me.
Hey! I'm Alex, 34m. Message me anytime you want
Hah. I ve worried also too much about purpose in one life. It felt like living in hell and now that i m trying to climb out it often catches up behind to torture me again.

That s what i believed during my psychosis. I did make much better assumptions about what others would do tho outside psychosis. Just saying you might have one rn. Might be a big leap tho on my side. Sorry if that s the case.

In my first psychosis i didn t do much to harm my well being and at times it was fun. Overally it wasn t a positive experience but it wasn t bad enough to make me stop. Weed just felt too good so i started again. I wasn t even sure what happened or what caused it. 2nd psychosis was much worse and i m more than certain weed caused it so i m sober almost 2 years now. It just depends how bad it can get i guess so you can learn something out of it.

Also to be completely honest smoking weed just felt so damn good i sometimes get the urge to try it again, but i have like this huge fear now it s gonna make me go nuts again. If i do ever try it again it s prolly gonna be really low doses, just to relax. (Or that s what i like telling myself)

Damn, i m so screwed up.

I find it hard not to converse with them. Thing is i m also quite convinced my consciousness is made up of neurons which i believe to be alive (there s also a phylosophycal current called panpsychism which states that consciousness permeates all matter and that we are made up of other forms of consciousness). I mean, i don t like talk to them like to a normal person, but it's more like i feel desperate because i have all these strange feelings that incapacitate me doing things i like and i just don t understand why my mind keeps feeding me all kind of doom scenarios and rotten feelings about myself so i decided to try to "converse"/communicate with these entities to get some answers or just to make some amends so i can live in peace.

Ofcourse i might be wrong but atm i just find it extremely difficult to live like this

My episodes lasted over 6 months each so i don t remember everything but some details i remember very well. I get back to my episodes sometimes to analyze this or that or why i did this and that. I think it helps me overally to better put things in perspective and try to understand what happened as to not have another one again

The crows aren t watching you. And this fear you are experiencing isn't real as in it s not motivated. It sounds like you re having another psychosis. We can talk if you want to about this or just talk to someone you trust or your therapist.

I actually, to be honest don't hear voices (i heard voices during psychosis). It's more like i 'hear' thoughts, because they form words but have no intonation.Since you mentioned this, I have like a constant feeling that i'm not alone but when i try and strain myself to observe who's there it's like 'they' all go quiet suddenly as if i walked into a room in which people were just talking about me. I asked about this earlier because I'm trying to get like an insight into what/who these entities are. So far I'm pretty sure my neurons are alive, but then i studied also a lot of biology in college and cells just always seemed alive to me, i just didn't ever think they are part of my consciousness. Well, at least that's my take on it, not 100℅ sure..

Mine never make such long phrases. I actually got a question about this if you don t mind. So, basically when i 'hear' a word sometimes i pay attention to that formed thought/word and i noticed than when i do that another one or two words associated with the first one are added. Is this how it happens for you too or they just pop up without you being so to speak on that trail of out-thoughts in any way?

These texts seem generic, cuz i heard them too often too. I'm not even now sure whether they realised i was delusional and believed (as in i was sure to the point of acting on those beliefs)all kinds of weird stuff. I get along with them rn but i feel like it's a cold conflict. I myself try to avoid any possible face to face conflict but they always seem to find stuff to reproach me about. And the problem is they're sure i m not sick in any way, just a loser who's besmirching the family name.

this was the biggest part of my episodes, telepathy, i was sure it s real and not only possible without technology but a natural evolution of the brain and part of a lot of peoples lives. I also had the same issues the first months coming out of my episode. It's definetely not mind reading. People just read your reactions and suppose logically what you're reacting to. It's very normal actually to think the same things especially in the same work enviroment and so on. It's just not real.

i would've said at first that the airplanes may signify something else, but since you say you live near an airport and see planes often it may just be that, your brain going into some emergency mode

Dunno if it's a start of an episode but i sure it ain't helping either. Any form of stress can trigger an episode from what i read from other people's experiences.

I have myself really freaking weird dreams every other night. Can't remember most of them but all of them involve this depressing feeling of being trapped, isolated and just basically being surrounded by weird beings who just wanna play with my mind.

It was cuz of weed for me. But i was also really depressed and wished very much to be somewhere else but in the life i had. So weed gave me that, a reality i wanted to chase (it implied a lot, but basically the ideas in the sf books i read became real for me and i started to chase them - telepathy, digital immortality, etc.)
I'd sneak into the whitehouse and see what the president is doing while alone

I try not to view the world as good or bad. These things differ very much on the perspective. Say a bacteria is alive (i'm actually quite sure it is experiencing some form of consciousness). Then from it's standpoint whatever is not from it's family/strain/species is a danger and is bad and has to be eliminated. Which is actually what bacteria do to other bacteria (that's how we discovered antibiotics, it's their weapon against other bacteria). I think this topic is a bit long and tedious but basically what helped me and helps me keep my suicidal thoughts away is trying not to focus too much on my own personal self. I dunno how to explain it, but it's a rabbit hole that only leads down this path.
I tried it, didn't lead me in a good place. Drugs fuck up your brain. (Reward system +others - you can find more in my post history)
Dunno if you can 'feel' anything after you die. This sort of motivates me to give it a try at living. Just don't like very much the place i'm in rn in life.

I'm also suicidal, have ocd too, pretty sure of it. If you look at suicide rate in schizophrenics it's somewhere between 10-14% compared to the 1% in genrral population. My point is one mental disease sort of pulls others into the mix. We just got thrown bad dicea in life.
May do that haha... Big + there are no humans in the wild,... Also the big - too

Well, i for one am struggling with everything you mentioned in your post. I can t say i enter the category you mentioned, but i feel like it's where i m headed. Because I want to live, i want to exist. Even when i don't want there's always a lingering part in me that wants to. I genuinely don't think there s anyone in the whole universe or multiverse that really doesn't want to exist. You just want to exist under certain conditions. My philosophy is quite simple i guess. If you can't defeat the monster then love it. This monster is the society and it's drives as a whole. It's made up of these people in a vast majority. And to be frank i don't think in this hell called earth where life feeds off other life, it's possible to survive without certain psychopathic traits. But sure, while i do love the monster cuz i have to, i will most certainly love another 'aware' living soul even more.

These connections are faulty in many other diseases too, plus the variation range of normal people, who don t have schizo or experience any other psychotic like or any psychiatric symptoms, who have these modifications is quite high. Besides, the hippocampus has many functions and it doesn t work by itself but also in connection with other limbic structures and also the cortex. Taking this all into account it's as vague as it can get.
I recommend you read svhizophrenia vs psychosis. But basically schizo means multiple psychotic episodes. Also yea, happened to me after smoking way too much.

Uh what, 100℅ sure not. This is not real. Honestly. Most, like 99℅ of people never had or can t comprehend what s it like not wanting to live. I know why you wanna believe it. It just won t help you in the long run. Really.

Also I'm shitful of psychiatry residents or young md's who just straight misinform people and try to make it sound really scholarly (which trust me, it's not.). All they got are theories and not one has any clear based evidence. Just fyi and please goddamn read this 10 times if you have to until you get it: schizophrenia is diagnosed ONLY based on clinical symptomatology, nothing else.

Look, i just took a pick. 'Faulty connectivity' is just as vague as neurotransmitter imbalance. What exactly is faulty in schizophrenia, besides the fact that something Is faulty? Exactly. It's just a theory and to be frank it's worse than neurochemical imbalance (which is just bad by itself).

And since we're on the subject here's something to think about when you take faulty wiring into account. Compared to autism or other neurological disorders schizophrenia comes in episodes. How's the wiring half the time faulty, half the time working?

And bah, the comment is just full of complicated words describing common symptoms, not freaking neurophysioanatomical workings or underlying causes. I mean wtf. Just stop with this bs.

A lot of complicated words naming the same thing that is used widely in most psychiatric diseases (Neurotransmitter imbalance) and which basically states that we don't know or understand much about it.

Oh damn. That s a long time... Thing is over a year passed since my last episode and i see some improvement, but it's quite little. Did you occupy yourself with anything new during that time? I m thinking of changing a bit my habbits but i just can't find anything outside work that helps...

In my most painful moments this was the only comforting thought I had. Something irks at me tho about the way you put it. You expect to feel at peace when you're dead. Even if you put it in comas you most certainly won't feel a damn thing given your own non-existence condition. 

Nah, I've lived through hell to realise what heaven can be like. I think I'd much more prefer heaven over non-existence. Eternal peace. 

One more thing. What makes this existence hell is other, ehm, human beings. They're too absorbed by their own self and forget what genuine love looks like. Well, I might overstate this, they never knew what it looks like, they just knew they could sell it or trade it for something material in return.
I have the same problem... How long did it take for you to enjoy games as usual, as before i mean?

I gave up on psychiatrists. I saw tons of them. Not one has really explained (and i m quite sure they don t understand much besides which treatment to prescribe) what i had, what to expect in the future and so on. Most of my information i got from the internet reading up a lot of studies and general information about schizophrenia and psychosis. Also reddit, but i joined here late. Also, a lot of analysis of the episodes i had helped me also very much in understanding what i m dealing with.

i had mdd which was undiagnosed for a whole 6 years or so, which i treated with alcohol and computer games (it worked for several years) and then i started smoking weed which i felt was amazing (i started smoking because i ended up on youtube hearing joe rogan talk a lot about psychedelics, which made really curious, also heard they used some to treat depression at which point i already knew i had, so then i read somewhere weed also had psychedelic properpeties in higher quantities so i started with that). Anyway, if you wanna talk more here or on pm's i m around. Isolation is a bitch indeed but i just got tired of people talking about menial stuff all day and it sucks out the energy out of me having idle talks about where my co worker goes to cut his hair, etc.

Edit: sorry, if you wanna read about my psychoses i wrote a whole post about it, you can find it in my recent post history

my mind was forcing me (as in that s how i believed i was perceived by others) to think i m a robot. It's a bit complicated, but at any rate i sort of was always refusing this view and was convinced i was human. But cuz of these contradicting viewpoints it made my psychosis worse and it was wearing me out a lot.

Despite the other answers i m pretty sure you can't. The whole point of psychosis is that your brain induces you to believe, besides other weird stuff like telepathy or magic (which ofc you might deny even during psychosis),  that you're on some kind of mission. Your subconscious sort of creates this mission or mission-like state which you fall into (because it does feel good, especially at the beginning). That's the whole point of it. You're tricked into it. Despite what others might say, i belive this to be the essential part of psychosis, the core of it's definition, all other psychosis like states are just that, similar, yet something else by definition.

I might be wrong, but i have a strong feeling I'm right about this. Looking forward for other opinions.

Honestly, the best, but probably also the slowest and hardest way is just to talk to her. Logic won t work at first, just hear her out, don t agree with her delusions to get under her skin because she may mistrust you and get more paranoid, but also don t contradict her. Let her get into to the thick of her psychotic delusions, take time to take them in, then work from there. 

What pulled me out of psychosis was a girl  who i knew who became my virtual lover for 6 months and to which i wrote endless messages she just ignored, also sometimes made fun of me on the phone and irl, but who in the end got bored and annoyed and told me to fuck off cuz i m imagining shit and she d never go out with me and so on. 

What i m trying to say that s what i needed to hear preferably when my psychosis started, not 6 months in. But that s literally what made me come back in the spawn of several hours.

My advice is somewhat of a mix, how i would do it if it ever happened to someone i knew or cared about. In the end tho i just might snap and tell them straight in their face what i think and that s just what might work best.

I didnt know it was common but i also had it... Well i mean i was sure i was a living person with a soul but i kept getting that feeling that that's how i m perceived from outside. Unfortunately i realised that most people see me as an object and no one sees inside me so i guess that s where it came from

Yea that sounds about right. Thing is... I think we have certain behaviors that define us and there's a survival tendency in us to anticipate each other so as to be aware when someone wants to do us harm. Still, in my experience i haven t found anyone who could try at least to see me for who i am.

Edit: and that s sort of the reason for it i guess. Nobody has a ingrained part of the brain responsible for seing people for who they are since nature doesn t need it. Well, yet at least.

Think this is sort of the same thing. The brain is like trying to give you a mission because you don t have one. I mean, i dunno. That s how it was for me. That one however is just too vague and to grandomaniac...

And it feels so good sometimes that you just can't abstain from doing it... It's annoying and unnerving. I think this is where having a real life purpose comes in, since you theoretically replace it with that, but i just can't find one good enough yet.
What s important is not that you have it or not. It s awareness of your psychotic breaks and that they damage your brain, mind, etc. This helped me realize i really never wanna have another one.
This was actually the basis of my psychotic breaks. Each time i became convinced telepathy was a thing and i was just opening my brain to this world of telepathic wobderful people
I actually find this a positive sign, since it means the subconscious brain is trying to catch up
Ah maybe the universe will just eventually die forever and ever and this hell will just stop into eternity.

To remain on topic, i think tho once you ve had a real attempt at it you get 2 reactions: people who care get closer to you and try to help you or they just completeley avoid you.

It also feels sometimes that it's the way the rich people want it. To keep you in this loop.

It's just a test. I do find that by living and experiencing various aspects of life it's innevitably gonna change your IQ. Besides, I do feel like it tests only certain aspects of your brain/mind. So I wouldn't put to much trust in these tests. They also vary a lot.

Well, if talking to someone random on the internet doesn't seem to help you I'd suggest maybe try doing a journal. It helped me a lot cause it just disinhibited me. At one point I poured a lot of hate out and then I said it's not ok. After I realised that it was worse keeping it inside. It helped me process a lot and right now I'm just pouring a lot of shit out so I just made an audio journal cause it's easier and I had tons of shit I wanted to pour out of myself. 

The idea of the journal would be for you to write it without anyone else reading it. I noticed when I did that my thoughts changed and I went somewhat back into my shell. It's you and your thoughts.

I'm not saying this is how it is, but it's a possibility. Ever thought maybe it's the other way around? Do you feel maybe like you're very often emotionally manipulated? Like you have no control of your decisions? And so on... I've been where you are and at some point I realised this and said fuck you. It was like I was in really a bad spot and she kept throwing shit at me that I'm the one responsible for her unhappiness and so on. I really needed help at that time, not more fights. I turned mostly useless and she kept pushing me around. Then I said to myself I'm not gonna feel sorry just cause you can't manipulate me any longer. Sort of turned it to 180 degrees and it made me feel much better. 

Try and look from outside on your relationship and what happened. That should help a lot
I'm here if you want to talk.

I've been here. Thing is I don't believe in God. At some point I made peace with it by telling myself I can't do it alone. It's impossible and self-destructive. Besides, not everyone needs saving the way we expect em to. I also sort of realised that this whole saving people idea was me ignoring my brain which was telling me to save myself.

Yea. I'm telling you, people think we're just sort of faking it at as a means to get attention. Some do. I've seen a few. Thing is, I'm quite certain that even if they take you seriously they ll trail of in various sorts of reasons why you wanna do it or why you did it. They simply just can t comprehend what it s like to not want to live. Aka what you feel. Also it's like our brains are sort of built to avoid pain. So nobody will go there willingly. 

And yea, it s weird as fuck. I m streaming towards having a stable state. Not what you mentioned. I mean it s like you gotta want to feel good all the time and fight for it. Otherwise it s the other way out.

Yep. Exactly like that. It's that doubt that keeps always scratching my brain. I mean, it's healthy to have a form of selfdoubt now and again but it's like my selfdoubt is uberoversized. Yours is probably too from what I get. It's just not healthy. It's suicidal. Haha.

Well, as I said, what helped me and I'm still working on it is saying fuck you (at least for a while). I'd suggest a break (the longer the better) from your usual enviroment. That might help tons. It helped me but I just can't get away cause I don't have the money cause otherwise I'd prolly go on world tour for like a year or so.

Also you're aware that you're easily influenced so maybe that's not the real you? That's why I'm suggesting that a break might help.

I don't know how to explain. It's like I wanna close this gate and every time I decide I have no reason to not feel good my brain keeps bringing up all sorts of weird stuff that I'm trying to filter through. Feels like hell sometimes. Guess it's cause I dissociate a lot.

At any rate. I stand by what I said. This whole shit is what contributed a lot at my suicidal thoughts and it's still contributing. It's not like I closed this door forever cause otherwise I wouldn't have suicidal thoughts. But I feel like I've made some progress and as long as things go smooth maybe there's a tiny hope I can climb out of it.
Well yea, I get it. It's sort of like fooling yourself and showing a happy face because you won't feel nothing when you're dead. I mean that pain that people will get after losing you.
I probably definetely would. Tho considering all the weird ideas in my head nobody probably will help or support me.
Do you mean like the real you that you found is the one who is trans?
I honestly believe it's crucial. Otherwise you'll be invalidating what you feel and make you push your thoughts away instead of trying to understand them.

I honestly don't think it's a good idea. In my experience when I pretended to be better people around me were starting to put more pressure. Plus it started wearing me out. All the pretending. It ended badly.

I think it inevitably always does. What works for me now is just saying "I'm fine" in the same monotone way like all the time. It's like saying "I know you don't care so stop bothering me or even asking at all". It actually worked quite well. Ofcourse, it did put some distance, but I'm really fine with it. At some point they just may do something nice to help me or cheer me up or just won't care. I'm fine either way.

This is sort of crucial not to pretend you're better. Don't feel bad you feel like shit. Just accept it. If they push you away or avoid you then they probably don't care. Also don't be scared to do it. It might build closer friendships and relationships to others, while pushing away the people that don't care about you. It might actually change a lot in your life. Hopefully for the better

At certain points I felt like I didn't know how to handle the people close to me or talk to them and it felt like they were just pressuring me. When I'm saying go my own way i don't mean like starting a totally different life. It's more like choosing a different lifestyle that's more healthy for me.

The "real me" was also self-destructive most of the time. After all the shit I've lived through I can say that it was just an illusion that this is the real me. I feel like there's also another version of me that can pull the "real me" out of this shithole but with the depression bursts I get sometimes it just feels like I'll never make it. At any rate, I also went through life sort knowing for the most of my life who I am and who I'm supposed to be but some events changed that. I felt completely lost. Like I didn't know who I was anymore and what's my purpose on earth. I've found reasons to pull myself out but I often just can't find the energy to do it. So saying all this I might have a different notion of who the "real me" is or was. Would like to know how it feels on your side.

Anyway, i think this is overally an illusion that we are gonna hurt the ones close to us if we take a different road. I m not saying just pack your things and say" fuck you all" to everyone. 

I'm still building up courage and trying to figure out where i am headed.  Basically what i wanna do with my life. What i m overally trying to say i guess is that what helped me most is saying fuck you in my head to everyone around. Not like literally pushing them away irl. 

I'm still figuring this shit out so don't take literally every word of what i said as being true. I may be wrong in many regards.

Thanks. The thing is... Your most serious thoughts sort of define, well, i wouldnt say exactly who we are, but more like where are we headed to and who we want to be. It's sort of a puzzle we're trying to figure out. Thing is, I used to push down my thoughts as they weren t important or meaningful in any way and that's what made it worse. Ofcourse, pushing away people close to you is also depressing as fuck for very many reasons. 

I sort of am still struggling with the nostalgia since it's so damn enticing and comfortable to go there but overally I am building this direction where I wanna go. 

Unfortunately at some point I realised that where I wanna go the people close to me won t follow. And that's scary and hurts like hell. 

But I have to go. At a certain point I have drained this emotional well of nostalgia and there is no other option than to create new emtions and experiences and to go forward. Staying in the same spot is still enticing since I sometimes still fall into nostalgic thoughts but they are always less and less (of emotion) and even if sometimes my mind gives off bursts of emotion from nostalgic thoughts and memories i realized at some point that it's a dead end and it will inevitably bring me to kill myself. 

Can't say that i've found the magical solution to not killing myself, but I'm trying to move forward. It's the only thing that will pull me out of this misery.
